confirmed: Read the complete markdown conversion, including Appendices A-H; checked the relevant methods, rubrics and numerical tables directly in the 64-page PDF (PDF pp. 1-64).

All eight outcomes use ratings of submissions or chat transcripts by two blinded, experienced education/psychology researchers, supporting expert_raters and scored_on_output=true (PDF pp. 9-10, section 3.7; p. 32, Appendix C).
S1-O1 is the creative-task component of individual performance gain: post-task minus baseline rubric scores, standardized before analysis (PDF p. 11, section 3.9; p. 52, Table 28).
S1-O1 overall_creativity is supported by the creative-writing total score and its originality, elaboration and coherence dimensions (PDF p. 11, Table 6; p. 33, Table 9).
S1-O2 novelty matches the originality rubric, which scores novel elements, surprising plots and freedom from predictable genre conventions (PDF p. 33, Table 9, Originality column).
S1-O3 elaboration matches rated detail about characters, setting, events and the story world (PDF p. 33, Table 9, Elaboration column).
S1-O4 usefulness matches narrative quality: logical consistency, connected story elements and cohesive construction (PDF p. 33, Table 9, Coherence column; codebook section 6, usefulness).

S1-O1 through S1-O4 concern Phase C individual submissions after the AI-containing group discussion, supporting immediate after_ai and no concurrent AI teammate (PDF pp. 5-6, section 3.2 and Figure 2; p. 11, section 3.9).
S1-O1 through S1-O4 use participant as the unit: the paper classifies pre/post rubric performance as individual-level, with group clustering in the gain model (PDF pp. 11-13, sections 3.9 and 3.11).

S1-O5 is transcript-scored discussion quality, averaging three group-level dimensions; other correctly distinguishes this process composite from story creativity (PDF pp. 11-12, section 3.9; p. 33, Table 8).
S1-O6 scores idea sharing, explanation and participation on a five-point rubric; it is not an idea count or a cross-person similarity statistic (PDF p. 33, Table 8, Idea generation & sharing column).
S1-O7 scores acknowledgement, development and integration of group members' contributions, supporting an other interaction-process construct (PDF p. 33, Table 8, Collaborative engagement column).
S1-O8 scores discussion progress, integration and shared understanding, supporting other rather than correct-answer convergent performance (PDF p. 33, Table 8, Progression & synthesis column).

S1-O5 through S1-O8 are produced during Phase B with AI agents participating continuously, supporting with_ai, AI available=yes and immediate timing (PDF pp. 5-6, section 3.2 and Figure 2; pp. 11-12, section 3.9).
S1-O5 through S1-O8 have team units; S1-O5 n_units=572 is explicitly the pooled all-task model count, as the form explains (PDF pp. 12-13, sections 3.9 and 3.11; p. 47, Table 24).
No recorded measure operationalizes similarity between different people's outputs; the group rubric is not a homogenization measure (PDF p. 33, Tables 8-9; codebook sections 1 and 6).
S1-O1: all five contrasts' primary and BDI-controlled coefficients, CR2 SEs, degrees of freedom, p-values, EMMs and EMM intervals exactly match the PDF (PDF pp. 52-54, Tables 28-29 and 31).
S1-O1: every reported treatment and control participant count matches the Creative Writing column (PDF p. 6, Table 2).
S1-O5: all five human-control contrasts' primary and BDI-controlled coefficients, CR2 SEs, degrees of freedom, p-values, EMMs and EMM intervals exactly match the PDF (PDF pp. 47-49, Tables 24-26).
S1-O1 and S1-O5 correctly use Creative as the reference task and H3 as the reference condition; directions follow Holm-adjusted CR2 tests (PDF pp. 47 and 52, Tables 24 and 28 and their notes).

S1-O5: Table 37 really prints 3.52 (0.12), Holm p<.001, for H2_S minus H2_C at both Creative BDI levels; the form preserves its exploratory status and verification caveat (PDF p. 57, Table 37 and section G.5).

S1-O2 through S1-O4 and S1-O6 through S1-O8 have dimension-level reliability but no separately printed arm means or effects; their empty contrasts do not omit reported subscale estimates (PDF p. 11, Table 6; pp. 38-64, Appendices E-H).
S1-O1 and S1-O5 are explicitly included among the paper's primary outcomes (PDF p. 15, Figure 3 caption).

No additional qualifying outcome was found: creativity-related survey items are self-reports, and linguistic mediation uses AI-only language features rather than human creativity or cross-person diversity (PDF pp. 8-9, section 3.6 and Table 4; pp. 13-14, section 3.12; pp. 59-64, Appendix H).
S2 reports perceived AI humanness only, providing no omitted human creative-output outcome (PDF p. 8, section 3.5).

Criterion 3 holds independently of the discussion-process measures because participants' individual movie plots received creativity rubric scores from blinded researchers (PDF pp. 9-11, sections 3.7 and 3.9; p. 28, Appendix A.3; p. 33, Table 9).
summary: The full-text and PDF checks support all eight outcomes' coding and the reported numerical entries, with no omitted qualifying outcome identified. Criterion 3 holds because blinded researchers scored participants' individual stories for originality, elaboration, and coherence.
